chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father asked him, and I was present, about a man who married a woman, and she was brought to him, but he did not touch her and did not reach her until he divorced her. Is there a waiting period (iddah) upon her from him? He said: 'The waiting period is from the water (seminal discharge).' It was said to him: 'So if he copulated with her in the vagina but did not ejaculate?' He said: 'When he entered (the penis) into her, the ritual bath (ghusl), the dower (mahr), and the waiting period (iddah) become obligatory.'

key_terms.أَدْخَلَ: To enter (specifically the penis into the vagina)
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (iddah) for a divorced or widowed woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on waiting period and dower if a man divorces his wife after entering the vagina but before ejaculation?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between mere entry and full consummation, ruling that vaginal entry alone obligates the complete dower (mahr), ritual bath (ghusl), and waiting period (iddah), even without ejaculation. This establishes the principle that physical union, not just procreation, defines the marital bond's legal consequences in Shia fiqh. The hadith underscores the importance of precise physical criteria in determining financial and ritual obligations upon divorce.
